scenes.title: One order. One accountable flow.

beats.text: A business orders connectivity. Instead of disconnected handoffs, one guarded supervisor coordinates five specialist agents.
The goal: less rework, faster activation, and a customer who knows what happens next.

scenes.banner: One order identity / explicit handoffs / bounded recovery / human authority
scenes.takeaway: ONE SUPERVISOR. FIVE SPECIALISTS. A TRACEABLE PATH TO ACTIVATION.

scenes.title: Accept once. Never lose the handoff.
events: Invalid request -> submitter corrects before acceptance

beats.text: Intake saves the order and its event together. A stable request key prevents duplicate acceptance.
Invalid requests return for correction. Accepted work stays traceable, without another manual handoff.

scenes.takeaway: STABLE IDENTITY + ATOMIC SAVE = NO DUPLICATE ACCEPTANCE.

scenes.title: Catch errors before they become fallout.
events: Site or capacity problem -> correction or manager review

beats.text: Validation checks the site and capacity before planning. Catching bad references early prevents downstream rework.
A wrong site needs customer confirmation. Missing capacity needs manager review, not an invented approval.

scenes.takeaway: PREVENT AVOIDABLE REWORK AT THE START, NOT AFTER ALLOCATION.

scenes.title: Plan once. Keep every task linked.

beats.text: Decomposition turns an approved product into linked service and resource orders. No repeated rekeying.
Unsupported products stop at intake. Catalogue governance keeps new mappings under the accountable planner's control.

scenes.takeaway: CATALOGUE MAPPINGS REPLACE REKEYING AND MISMATCHED REFERENCES.

scenes.title: Check policy. Then allocate once.

beats.text: Provisioning rechecks capacity, risk and the change window, then allocates resources once.
A partner timeout activates recovery. A policy conflict takes a different path: human review.

scenes.takeaway: NO DUPLICATE ALLOCATION. NO POLICY BYPASS. NO FALSE SUCCESS.

scenes.title: Recover the known fault. Hand back.

beats.text: Recovery handles one allowlisted timeout, retries once, and hands control back to provisioning.
For faults outside that playbook, the delivery design requires service-desk integration and an accountable human owner.

scenes.takeaway: ONE ALLOWLISTED RETRY. BACK TO PROVISIONING. NEVER AN ENDLESS LOOP.

cards.title: KNOWN TIMEOUT

cards.title: RETRY ONCE

scenes.title: People own the high-risk decision.

beats.text: The service manager approves or rejects high-risk work. Every decision is audited.
Approval cannot create capacity. Partners cannot approve. Permitted work resumes its saved stage.

scenes.banner: Closed window -> audited release / capacity requires inventory resolution
scenes.takeaway: AUDITED APPROVAL OR REJECTION. PARTNERS CANNOT OVERRULE POLICY.

scenes.title: Close the loop with truthful status.
events: TR / EN portal updates -> order completed

beats.text: After activation, customer updates persist Turkish and English portal confirmations. Clear status reduces chasing.
The portal provides the customer record. Email and text delivery require integrated channel services and service-desk ownership.

scenes.takeaway: ACTIVATE FIRST. CONFIRM SECOND. LESS CHASING FOR THE CUSTOMER.

scenes.title: Shared contracts. The same guardrails.

beats.text: TM Forum inspired product and service contracts preserve linked handoffs. Authenticated partner tools enter the same guarded flow.
Customer integration defines the exact schemas and conformance acceptance. Partner access never bypasses policy or human authority.

scenes.takeaway: LINKED CONTRACTS. AUTHENTICATED PARTNER TOOLS. ONE GUARDED FLOW.

scenes.title: Keep the customer workload in Turkey.
events: Azure Local / approved operator site in Turkey
Local infrastructure + local services + controlled egress

beats.text: The residency architecture places the customer workload on Azure Local at an approved Turkish operator site.
Delivery requires supported local infrastructure, local inference, keys, logs and backups, with controlled egress and regulatory approval.

scenes.takeaway: BRING COMPUTE TO THE DATA. KEEP THE CUSTOMER DATA PLANE LOCAL.

scenes.title: Connect cloud services with a clear boundary.
events: Approved images in / approved metadata out

beats.text: External Azure services supply approved images, management and monitoring. Every metadata flow needs approval.
Where platform metadata must also stay local, evaluate eligible disconnected operations, with its local control plane and support requirements.

scenes.title: Less rework. Less waiting. More confidence.
events: Early checks + linked work + bounded recovery
Customer objectives / lead time, quality and visibility

beats.text: Early checks address avoidable rework. Linked identifiers remove rekeying. Durable handoffs and bounded recovery reduce unnecessary waiting.
The customer objective is simple: shorter delivery, fewer avoidable exceptions, and a clear, accountable path from order to activation.

scenes.takeaway: FOCUS ON LEAD TIME, FIRST-TIME-RIGHT COMPLETION AND CUSTOMER VISIBILITY.
